name: Adhara
description: A bright giant of type B2 II 124 parsecs away, 10.7 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Narrabri intensity interferometer.

paper.credit: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417

radius.source: Computed here, not printed by a paper: 10.7 +/- 0.69 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.8 +/- 0.05 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 8.05 +/- 0.14 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP)

temperature.source: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 52089: effective temperature 20990 +/- 760 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 33579: RV 27.3 +/- 0.4 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 33579: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 8.05 +/- 0.14 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A bright giant of type B2 II, 124 parsecs away: 10.7 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.8 milliarcseconds, which at its distance is 10.7 solar radii, and its surface is at 20,990 K.
text.locator: Tables 1 and 6, HD 52089: MK type, limb-darkened diameter, effective temperature
